topic.subject: social
topic.title: Electoral politics
topic.scope: why elections, constituencies, reserved constituencies, voters' list, Election Commission, campaigns, model code

misconceptions.statement: Elections are only held to choose the most popular or famous person.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate political leadership with celebrity status due to media coverage of rallies.
misconceptions.fix: Elections are a mechanism for citizens to choose representatives who will make laws and policies on their behalf.

probe.question: Why do we hold elections in India?
probe.wrong_answer: To see which leader is the most famous and loved by the people.

misconceptions.statement: Reserved constituencies mean that only people from that caste can vote there.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the eligibility of the candidate with the eligibility of the voter.
misconceptions.fix: In reserved constituencies, only candidates from specific groups can contest, but all registered voters in that area can cast their vote.

probe.question: Who can vote in a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes?
probe.wrong_answer: Only people belonging to the Scheduled Castes living in that area.

misconceptions.statement: The Election Commission works under the control of the ruling government.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that because the government pays for the election, it must control the agency conducting it.
misconceptions.fix: The Election Commission is an independent body that functions without the interference of the government or the ruling party.

probe.question: Who controls the Election Commission during an election?
probe.wrong_answer: The ruling party because they are in power.

misconceptions.statement: The Model Code of Conduct is a law that bans all political activity during elections.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret 'code' as a strict legal prohibition rather than a set of guidelines for fair conduct.
misconceptions.fix: The Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines to ensure fair play, not a total ban on political campaigning.

probe.question: What happens when the Model Code of Conduct is in force?
probe.wrong_answer: All political parties must stop campaigning and stay at home.
